decision: Authorize the integrity-hardening wave to write the files listed in affected_artifact_ids even though they fall outside the declared write_scope of any A-Z work package. This covers three categories: (1) canonical schema amendments that close contract defects — source_locator nullable page across six schemas plus source-span, node-contract executor_status, document-registration x-canonical-hash.field_sources, and retrieval-candidate x-canonical-identity exclusion_policy — of which document-registration and node-contract sit in C01's declared scope; (2) new verification gates under tests/contracts/** and tests/workflows/**, neither of which appears in any write_scope glob; (3) the integrity registries artifacts/work_packages/pin-supersessions.json, pin-census.json and receipt-invalidations.json, which belong to no package because they are cross-package by nature. This authorization does not reopen any sealed package, does not extend to remote or destructive operations, and does not grant push, merge or release authority.
rationale: An independent contract review (finding F10) established that these writes had no covering scope and no authority record, while the repository requires a resolving artifact for every implementation claim (manifests/development_manifest.yaml). The product owner was shown the finding verbatim, including that the affected files sit outside every declared scope and that schemas/document-registration.schema.json belongs to C01 rather than the B04 supersession the change was booked against, and instructed that all findings be remediated. The alternative — amending each package's write_scope in manifests/development_manifest.yaml — would edit a higher authority document to retroactively legalise work already done, which is the weaker record. A scope decision recorded at the point of the exception is the mechanism this repository already uses 46 times.
